subject: history_social
passage: Construction of the Appian Way, the first great Roman road, began in 312 BCE under the official Appius Claudius Caecus. The road, which eventually ______ more than 500 kilometers from Rome to the port of Brindisi on the Adriatic coast, was paved with tightly fitted blocks of stone and remained in use for centuries.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The clause beginning with "which" needs a complete verb of its own. The passage is in the past tense ("began," "was paved," "remained"), so the finite past-tense verb "stretched" is needed; the -ing, to-, and having- forms cannot serve as the main verb of a clause.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Having stretched" is a participle phrase, not a finite verb, so the clause is incomplete.
explanation.B: Correct. "Stretched" is a finite past-tense verb, completing the "which" clause and matching the other past-tense verbs.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "To stretch" is an infinitive and cannot act as the main verb of the "which" clause.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Stretching" is a participle, not a finite verb, so the "which" clause would have no main verb.
